Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — model fit / evals

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a shared plan: 

Summary from call:
- Primary workload: conversational assist for enterprise support (long context, value on latency under 300ms for p95).
- Throughput target: ~120 TPS peak across two regions; average closer to 30–40 TPS.
- Quality requirements: strict consistency on slot-filling and few-shot behavior; sensitive to hallucinations on invoice fields.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share Redwood-verified benchmark links and our recommended model variants for your prompt set (attached).
2) You’ll share a small representative prompt set and 100 example conversations (anonymized) — we can use those to run a quick fit/eval.
3) If the fit looks good, we’ll spin up a short Dedicated trial for a week to validate latency percentiles and throughput.

Attachments: acme-prompt-set.csv (sample format), redwood-profile-acmeai-v1.pdf (performance summary).

Can you confirm you’re comfortable sharing the anonymized examples? If so, I’ll get the evals started and loop in Alex to check latency tuning.

Best,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

2) We’re concerned about potential quality regressions after quantization. Do you have visibility into how often regressions occur across rollout windows?

samuel.lee@acme.ai
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — model fit / evals

Hi Sam — thanks for the questions. Linking the initial materials and answers below.

Quick recommendations (based on your throughput and latency goals):
- Redwood-llama-3-small (quantized profile q4f16): best starting point for cost-sensitive POC; expected p50 ~ 45ms, p95 ~= 180–220ms on our Dedicated r4 configs at 256-token context for conversational traffic; TPS in the 80–140 range when sharded across 2 GPUs.
- Redwood-llama-3-medium (fp16): if you need higher quality on invoice extraction, p95 ~ 120–160ms (higher cost).

Quality regressions & quantization: 
- We run Redwood-verified regressions against your prompt set during any quantization pipeline. Historically (across similar customers), regressions are rare but not impossible — we capture delta metrics on accuracy/F1 for the eval prompt set and flag any model variant with >2% regression for manual review.
- If a regression is flagged, the rollout is automatically paused and the model material is routed to our QA + applied ML team for a targeted calibration pass (can include alternative quantization bit-widths or small fine-tuning).

Benchmarks: 
- Redwood-verified performance profile (attached): includes TPS, p50/p90/p95 latency percentiles across real-world request mixes.
- Live dashboard (redwood console): https://console.redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-ai/compare?model=redwood-llama-3

Attached: redwood-profile-acmeai-v1.pdf (performance summary), acme-prompt-set.csv (sample format). I’ll also run the first fit using the anonymized examples once you send them.

Let me know if you want us to include packet traces or a flamegraph from the serving runtime for the p95 tail debugging — Alex can prep those.

Regards,
Dylan
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Lee <samuel.lee@acme.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — model fit / evals

Hi Sam — quick tech note from the runtime side.

If you expect many long-context sessions, we recommend testing with our "continuous KV caching" enabled — it preserves per-user KV-cache between messages and reduces compute per token. That typically drops p95 by ~25–40% for long sessions. Also, when you share the anonymized set, include typical sequence-length distribution so we can pick the right kernel/compilation profile.

If you want, we can also include an early A/B run with both q4f16 and fp16 variants to quantify quality delta on your invoice extraction evals.

Thanks,
Alex
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Samuel Lee <samuel.lee@acme.ai>

One small ask for the profile PDF: can you add a one-page summary showing p95 in ms for the recommended configs (table) — our infra team needs that for the evaluation ticket.

Sam
